finding: Two date fields contain recognized non-date workflow labels alongside explicitly unavailable values. No other unparseable text was found across the five audited date fields.
rule_tested: Classified each value in five date fields as a valid date, missing/blank, explicitly unavailable, recognized workflow status, or other unparseable text. Parsed dates using pandas to_datetime with format='mixed' and errors='coerce'.
evidence: PQ first sent to client: 7,643 valid dates (74.03%), 205 explicitly unavailable (1.99%), and 2,476 'Pre-PQ Process' workflow labels (23.98%). PO sent to vendor: 4,592 valid dates (44.48%), 328 explicitly unavailable (3.18%), and 5,404 'N/A - From RDC' workflow labels (52.34%). Scheduled delivery, delivered to client, and delivery recorded each contain 10,324 valid dates (100%). No other unparseable text was found. Workflow meanings have not been independently verified.
classification: Date-field exceptions classified; workflow semantics and business requirements not independently verified
recommended_action: Preserve original values. Confirm the meanings of 'Pre-PQ Process' and 'N/A - From RDC' against source documentation or a knowledgeable data owner. Keep workflow statuses separate from actual dates in downstream analysis; do not automatically replace them with missing values or impute dates.
validation_status: All five fields audited across 10,324 records. Counts reconcile to the full dataset; zero other unparseable values. Workflow semantics remain unverified.
next_validation: Seek source documentation or data-owner confirmation for the two workflow labels and the meaning of explicitly unavailable values. Reassess only if new evidence changes their interpretation.
priority_rationale: Priority should be assessed against business requirements and operational impact. Most non-date values are two recognized workflow labels, not arbitrary parsing failures. Their meanings remain unverified, so severity and priority are provisional.

finding: Pricing arithmetic differences and recorded-precision relationship
rule_tested: Tested pack price against unit price multiplied by units per pack using a $0.02 tolerance; then tested whether recorded unit price matches pack price divided by units per pack rounded to 2 decimals. Also tested line item value against quantity multiplied by pack price using a $0.02 tolerance, then tested whether line item value divided by quantity rounds to the recorded pack price.
evidence: Initial pack-price test: 7,774 of 10,324 records (75.30%) differed by more than $0.02 when comparing pack price with unit price multiplied by units per pack. A separate reverse-calculation test found that all 10,324 recorded unit prices matched pack price divided by units per pack, rounded to two decimals. Rounding unit price multiplied by units per pack brought only 90 of the 7,774 initial exceptions within $0.02. Separately, 549 records (5.32%) exceeded the $0.02 tolerance when comparing line-item value with quantity multiplied by pack price; all 549 passed the implied-pack-price rounding test. The source system's intended pricing method remains unconfirmed; these results do not establish a confirmed pricing defect or financial loss.
classification: Initial arithmetic exceptions investigated; no confirmed pricing error established
recommended_action: Document recorded-price precision and validate pricing using rules appropriate to the stored precision. Do not correct or reject records solely because multiplication of rounded prices differs from a recorded total. Confirm the calculation convention with source documentation if available.
validation_status: The reverse-calculation test matched recorded unit price to pack price divided by units per pack, rounded to two decimals, for all 10,324 records. The separate unit-price-times-UOM rounding test brought only 90 of the 7,774 initial exceptions within $0.02. All 549 line-value exceptions passed the implied-pack-price rounding test. Source-system pricing methodology remains unconfirmed.
next_validation: Retain the test outputs as evidence. Seek source documentation for the pricing calculation convention if available; do not reopen the same arithmetic hypothesis without new evidence.
priority_rationale: The 7,774 initial arithmetic differences are not confirmed pricing defects. The reverse-calculation relationship holds for all 10,324 records, but rounding unit price multiplied by units per pack brought only 90 initial exceptions within $0.02. No confirmed financial impact has been established. Retain as a low-priority documentation and source-methodology follow-up.
priority_status: Provisional - no confirmed pricing defect; low-priority follow-up pending source-methodology evidence

finding: Weight and freight fields mix numeric values, cross-record references, and explanatory text.
rule_tested: Classified all 10,324 records in weight (kilograms) and freight cost (usd) as numeric, blank, cross-record reference, or other explanatory/non-numeric text.
evidence: Weight: 6,372 numeric (61.72%), 2,445 cross-record references (23.68%), 1,507 other explanatory text (14.60%), and 0 blank. Freight: 6,198 numeric (60.03%), 2,445 cross-record references (23.68%), 1,681 other explanatory text (16.28%), and 0 blank. All 2,445 references in each field resolve to existing target records, and both fields reference the same target within each source record. Target ASN/DN document numbers match the extracted reference numbers in all 2,445 cases per field. No mismatches were found in the tested country, shipment mode, vendor, fulfilment method, product group, or delivered date fields. Seven references per field have different scheduled dates from their targets, although delivered dates match. Those seven pairs also differ in item description and quantity. Reference semantics and value-transfer rules remain unverified.
classification: Mixed-type operational fields; explanatory text and cross-record references are not automatically errors.
recommended_action: Preserve original values. Parse numeric values into separate derived fields using explicit rules. Keep explanatory categories distinct and validate documented value-transfer rules before deriving weight or freight from referenced records. Do not silently replace text with nulls or copy values automatically.
validation_status: Field classifications and tested reference links validated; operational meaning and value-transfer rules remain unconfirmed
next_validation: Seek source documentation or data-owner confirmation of how weight and freight should be interpreted when referenced from another record. Review the seven scheduled-date differences without copying or aggregating values automatically.
priority_rationale: Mixed numeric values, cross-record references, and explanatory text require explicit handling before reliable weight and freight analysis. DQ-07 covers a related reference-resolution aspect. Assess both findings together and avoid double-counting overlapping records or impacts.
priority_status: Provisional - operational impact and business rules remain unconfirmed; assess jointly with DQ-07

finding: Weight and freight values contain references to other records
rule_tested: Extract referenced IDs and validate target existence and shipment identifiers.
evidence: There are 4,890 field-level reference occurrences across 2,445 source records: 2,445 in weight and 2,445 in freight. Both fields point to the same target ID in all 2,445 records. All target IDs exist, and the extracted ASN/DN document number matches the target record's ASN/DN in every reference. No mismatches were found in the tested country, shipment mode, vendor, fulfilment method, product group, or delivered date fields. Seven source-target pairs have different scheduled dates, item descriptions, and quantities, but matching delivered dates. The references are internally consistent on the tested fields; their operational meaning and rules for transferring weight or freight remain unverified.
classification: Cross-record reference integrity validated for tested fields; business semantics unresolved
recommended_action: Document reference semantics and prevent automatic copying or double-counting until rules are confirmed.
validation_status: Target existence, shared target IDs, and ASN/DN document-number matches validated; reference meaning remains unconfirmed
next_validation: Confirm whether references represent shipment-level values, shared values, or another documented convention. Assess jointly with DQ-06 and avoid double-counting the same underlying issue.
priority_rationale: Cross-record references may require documented value-transfer rules, but their meaning and downstream impact remain unconfirmed. This finding overlaps with DQ-06; assess jointly rather than treating it as an independent affected population.
priority_status: Provisional - reference semantics and impact unconfirmed; assess jointly with DQ-06

finding: Missing dosage is concentrated in diagnostic test products, with a small additional group of malaria records.
rule_tested: Count missing dosage values overall and by product group, sub classification, item description, brand, and dosage form.
evidence: 1,736/10,324 records (16.82%) have missing dosage. HRDT: 1,728/1,728; MRDT: 8/8; ARV: 0/8,550. By sub classification: HIV test 1,567/1,567; HIV test - Ancillary 161/161; Malaria 8/30 (26.67%); Adult, Pediatric, and ACT have no missing dosage. Test kit (1,575/1,575) and Test kit - Ancillary (161/161) have 100% missing dosage.
classification: Missingness pattern established and concentrated in diagnostic products; requirement and impact unconfirmed.
recommended_action: Confirm whether dosage is applicable and mandatory for each product type, especially diagnostic kits and ancillary items. Investigate the eight malaria records individually. Preserve original values and do not impute dosage without authoritative product or source documentation.
validation_status: Overall missing count and product-level distribution investigated. Counts reconcile across the reported product groups, sub classifications, and dosage forms. Business requirements and downstream impact remain unconfirmed.
next_validation: Verify dosage requirements against authoritative product specifications or source documentation; assess the eight malaria records and downstream analytical use.
priority_rationale: Missing dosage affects 16.82% of records; requiredness and analytical impact need confirmation.

finding: Zero unit prices observed across 103 records, including a concentrated product-specific pattern in HIV safety-lancet records.
rule_tested: Identify records where unit price equals zero.
evidence: 103/10,324 records have unit_price = 0; 71 are HRDT and 32 are ARV. Of these, 85 have positive pack prices and 86 have positive line-item values. For the product 'HIV, Lancet, Safety, for HIV Test kits, 100 Pcs', 58/65 records have unit_price = 0.00 and pack_price = 0.01, while seven records have unit_price = 0.05 and pack_price = 5.00. The 58 zero-unit-price records have line-item values equal to quantity multiplied by 0.01; the seven positive-unit-price records have line-item values equal to quantity multiplied by 5.00.
classification: Observed zero-price anomaly; business meaning and correctness not independently established.
recommended_action: Retain original values. Investigate the product-specific pricing convention using authoritative source documentation or confirmation from the data owner. Do not automatically replace zero prices or classify the records as financial errors without supporting evidence.
validation_status: Counts and product-level pattern investigated. The reason for the two observed price scales remains unverified; no confirmed financial loss or pricing error established.
next_validation: Seek source-system documentation or data-owner confirmation; then determine whether zero unit prices are valid under the original pricing convention.
priority_rationale: Zero unit prices affect 103 records, with a concentrated pattern for one product. Business meaning and financial impact remain unverified, so priority is provisional.
priority_status: Provisional - reassess after remaining investigations and impact review

finding: Potential duplicate shipment records with identical non-ID attributes.
rule_tested: Compare repeated-quantity candidates across all non-ID fields.
evidence: Four candidate duplicate pairs involving eight records were identified by comparing all 32 fields other than the unique record ID. Pairs: 10692/11246 (SO-1291, DN-686); 11882/12792 (SO-716, DN-770); 12146/12147 (SO-710, DN-488); and 43250/68128 (SCMS-200920, ASN-21751). Each pair matches across all 32 non-ID fields, including shipment references and recorded dates.
classification: Four candidate duplicate pairs identified; duplicate status unconfirmed.
recommended_action: Retain all records pending review. Reconcile each candidate pair against original shipment documentation or the authoritative source system. Do not delete or deduplicate records solely on matching attributes.
validation_status: Candidate pairs reproduced in a repeatable scan of 10,324 records. Four pairs and eight records match across all 32 non-ID fields. Whether these represent accidental duplicate entries or legitimate separate transactions remains unverified.
next_validation: Obtain independent shipment-level documentation or source-system confirmation for the four candidate pairs before deciding whether any records should be deduplicated.
priority_rationale: Four pairs involving eight records match across all 32 non-ID fields, including shipment references. Potential reporting impact warrants review, but duplication and financial impact have not been established.
priority_status: Provisional - duplicate status and business impact remain unconfirmed

finding: Missing line-item insurance values with variation across product groups and shipment characteristics.
rule_tested: Count missing line-item insurance values overall and compare missingness by product group, sub classification, shipment mode, country, vendor, fulfillment route, vendor incoterm, and managing office.
evidence: 287/10,324 records (2.78%) have missing insurance. ARV: 209/8,550 (2.44%); HRDT: 78/1,728 (4.51%). By shipment mode: 106/360 records with missing mode also have missing insurance (29.44%); Air: 181/6,113 (2.96%). By fulfillment: From RDC 169/5,404 (3.13%); Direct Drop 118/4,920 (2.40%). Country examples: Zambia 45/683 (6.59%), Côte d'Ivoire 63/1,083 (5.82%), Mozambique 38/631 (6.02%). Median line-item value was 32,000 for records with missing insurance and 30,400 for records with recorded insurance.
classification: Missingness count and descriptive patterns established; insurance applicability, cause, and financial impact remain unconfirmed.
recommended_action: Confirm whether insurance is required for each shipment and whether missing values mean not applicable, unknown, or unrecorded. Investigate the overlap with missing shipment mode. Preserve original values and do not impute zero or infer financial loss without evidence.
validation_status: Missing count established and compared across available shipment characteristics. Business meaning, cause, and financial impact have not been independently confirmed.
next_validation: Review source documentation and insurance rules; examine records with both missing shipment mode and insurance; confirm whether missing insurance should be treated as not applicable, unknown, or a completeness defect.
priority_rationale: Missing insurance values may affect insurance analysis; applicability and downstream impact need confirmation.
priority_status: Provisional - insurance applicability and impact unconfirmed
